source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Yayati tale (the story of Kacha). CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.71.25–58 and 1.72.1–5 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): FIRST DEATH: the danavas, seeing Kacha alone in the wood herding cattle, killed him, cut him as small as sesame grains and gave him to the jackals (shalavrika: 1.71.26: `first`; the jackals are on the tag, not voiced; they did it out of hatred of Brihaspati and to guard the knowledge: "to guard their priest's secret"); the cows came home without their herdsman; Devayani said: the fire-offering is not made, the sun has set, the cows have come without a herdsman, Kacha is not to be seen; he is surely killed or dead; without him I will not live (1.71.27–29: `cows`); Shukra: I bring the dead to life with the words "come here" (1.71.30); he used the samjivani and called, and Kacha appeared unharmed (1.71.31: `come`). SECOND DEATH: sent by Devayani for flowers he went to the wood and the danavas saw him (1.71.32); killing him a second time they burned him, ground him to powder and gave him to the brahmin himself in his wine (1.71.33: `second`); Shukra: he is killed even when revived; what can I do; do not grieve (1.71.35–36; not voiced); Devayani: I will not eat; I will go the way Kacha went (1.71.38); urged by her he called again, and Kacha, afraid for his teacher, answered softly from the belly (1.71.40–41: `belly`, the turn) and told how he came there (1.71.42–43); Shukra: only by the splitting of my belly could Kacha be seen (1.71.44); Devayani: two griefs burn me like fire: Kacha's destruction and your harm; if Kacha is lost I have no peace; if you are harmed I cannot live (1.71.45: `two`); Shukra: receive this life-giving knowledge; come out of my body as my son, and then look to what is right (1.71.46–48: `teach`); having received it Kacha split the belly and came out on the brahmin's right side like the moon on a full-moon night; seeing his teacher fallen he raised him (1.71.49–50: `out`); Shukra, deceived through wine, laid down that a brahmin who drinks liquor from that day loses his law (1.71.52–55: on a tag, not voiced); Kacha stayed a thousand years in all with his teacher and then, with leave, wished to go to the gods' home (1.71.58); as he set out Devayani spoke (1.72.1–5: the cliffhanger). CE AGAINST THE VULGATE AND THE CATALOG PLAN: the plan's title was "Kacha Dies Three Times" and its synopsis had three deaths. The constituted text has TWO (1.71.26 and 1.71.33). The death in which he is pounded and mixed into the ocean's water, and called back a second time, is star passage 701* (apparatus). The episode is retitled "Kacha Dies Twice" in the catalog, and the source line says so. The killing and the splitting are not shown: light opens.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

loop.hookQuestion: Who was killed twice and raised twice, and how?
loop.prevQuestion: Can a dead student be brought back?
loop.openQuestion: What did Devayani ask of Kacha?

strings.prevEpisodeTitle: The Secret of Reviving the Dead
strings.recapLine: A son of the gods' priest became the student of the asuras' priest.
strings.sourceLine: Adi Parva 1.71 · two deaths here; later tellings add a third · BORI Critical Edition

lines.note: COLD OPEN (a count; no fire): a violet wood: a herdsman's staff lies on the path among hoof prints, white cows walking away without him; a tilt up to the tree tops where a pale green light is gathering. The card low.

lines.text: To guard their priest's art of raising the dead, the asuras killed his student, Kacha.
lines.say: To guard their priest's art [p:60] of raising the dead, [p:150] the asuras killed his student, [p:150] Kacha.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top) (venom-violet): a rack focus from the dropped staff in the foreground to horned shapes closing over the place where he stood (plaque: Kacha · son of the gods' priest); then only the jackals' eyes, low among the trunks. Nothing of the killing is drawn (sub: cut small as sesame, given to the jackals · Adi 1.71.26).

lines.speaker: devayani
lines.text: "Father, the cows came home without him."
lines.say: Father, [p:150] the cows came home [p:80] without him.
lines.note: STORY 1 · THE CLOSE-UP (grief-blue: nightfall): Devayani's face fills the frame (plaque: Devayani · Shukra's daughter): watching the gate, hope; then the cows pass and no one follows: fear, the eyes filling.

lines.text: Her father, Shukra, called: Come! And Kacha stood there, whole.
lines.say: Her father, [p:60] Shukra, [p:80] called: [p:200] Come! [p:300] And Kacha stood there, [p:150] whole.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (thicket-shade; answers episode 59's question by 15 s): Shukra standing, white-haired, a hand flung out (plaque: Shukra · priest of the asuras; sub: he alone knew the art of raising the dead); a ring of pale green light opens in the air before him and Kacha steps out of it, looking at his own hands. A slow orbit.

lines.text: Next they burned him to powder, and stirred him into Shukra's wine.
lines.say: Next they burned him to powder, [p:200] and stirred him [p:60] into Shukra's wine.
lines.note: STORY 3 · NEW LIGHT (wrath-crimson): asura hands only, in red light: a pinch of grey ash falls into a gold cup; a tilt up: the cup is carried on a tray to the unsuspecting sage, who drinks (tag: Later tellings add a third death. The Critical Edition has two.).

lines.text: Shukra called again. Kacha answered softly, from inside his teacher's belly.
lines.say: Shukra called again. [p:400] Kacha answered softly, [p:200] from inside his teacher's belly.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 48 %) after a real silence (hearth-amber: one lamp; a lamp, not a fire): Shukra stands calling toward the dark door; then stops, and slowly looks down at himself, a hand going to his own belly, where a small green light pulses. The word of the turn: WITHIN.

lines.speaker: devayani
lines.text: "If he dies, I cannot bear it. If you die, I cannot live."
lines.say: If he dies, [p:120] I cannot bear it. [p:350] If you die, [p:120] I cannot live.
lines.note: STORY 5 (grief-blue): Devayani on her knees between the lamp and the door, turned to her father; her hands go out to him and stop (sub: Adi 1.71.45).

lines.speaker: shukra
lines.text: "Then learn my art, Kacha, and bring me back."
lines.say: Then learn my art, [p:120] Kacha, [p:250] and bring me back.
lines.note: STORY 6 (a second real silence before it; release-gold): Shukra seated, eyes closed, both hands over the light in his belly, his lips moving: he teaches the art to the one inside him; the green light turns gold as it learns.

lines.text: Kacha came out like a rising full moon, and raised his teacher.
lines.say: Kacha came out [p:80] like a rising full moon, [p:300] and raised his teacher.
lines.note: STORY 7 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (memory-indigo; answers the hook): a white disc of light swells from the seated sage's right side and fills the frame like a moon; out of it Kacha steps, whole; behind him the sage lies fallen; Kacha turns, raises a hand as his teacher did, and Shukra's eyes open. No wound is drawn: light opens. A crane up.

lines.text: When Kacha took his leave, Devayani had something to ask.
lines.say: When Kacha took his leave, [p:350] Devayani [p:60] had something to ask.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger; CE 1.71.58, 1.72.1): the garden at morning: Kacha with a traveller's staff and bundle, bowing farewell; Devayani steps into his path, flowers in her hair, a hand raised to stop him (tags, two seconds each: after a thousand years · Adi 1.71.58; Shukra then forbade wine to brahmins · Adi 1.71.54). The source line (top).
The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
